limit_order_match_in_progress.meaning: a limit order matching (partial or full) is being processed through _processLimitBidOrder or _processLimitAskOrder
limit_order_match_in_progress.checkpoint: before the zero-cost check during limit order matching

matched_amounts_disjoint_bits.meaning: the matched base amount and matched quote amount have no overlapping 1-bits (e.g., base = 256 and quote in 1..255, or 40 & 21)
matched_amounts_disjoint_bits.checkpoint: before the zero-cost check during limit order matching

matched_base_amount_nonzero.meaning: the matched base amount of the legitimate limit order match is nonzero
matched_base_amount_nonzero.checkpoint: before the zero-cost check during limit order matching

matched_quote_amount_nonzero.meaning: the matched quote amount of the legitimate limit order match is nonzero
matched_quote_amount_nonzero.checkpoint: before the zero-cost check during limit order matching

rejected_as_zero_cost_trade.meaning: the legitimate limit order match is rejected as a zero-cost trade
rejected_as_zero_cost_trade.checkpoint: during limit order matching when the zero-cost check is applied

traders_encounter_unexplained_failures.meaning: traders, especially algorithmic ones using round numbers, encounter unexplained failures

assumptions: The matched base and quote amounts are observable quantities of the legitimate limit order match at the zero-cost check checkpoint.

unresolved.description: The report does not quote the exact zero-cost check expression or its operands, so the rejection-as-zero-cost outcome is represented by a grounded Boolean rather than a numeric relation.
The report states the disjoint-1-bits condition only by example (base = 256 and quote in 1..255, or 40 & 21) without a general numeric definition, so it is encoded as a grounded Boolean.

limitations: The impact is potential; the impact_outcome Boolean records the reported possible unexplained failures rather than an inevitable outcome.
Caller identity and authorization for triggering limit order matching are not stated by the report and are not encoded.
Whether matched amounts are caller-supplied inputs or derived from order state is not specified; the plan treats them as observable match quantities.
